knownFailures.reason: oxlint's own JS plugin host fails with the anonymous 'Error running JS plugin.' on a binary expression chain of about 2800 levels or more (a 3000-term string concatenation), and production then drops every Vue Doctor finding for the file without a message. Not a rule defect; a real limit of the host. Lower priority, but a generated file of this shape is silently unlinted.

readManifest (src/plugin/supply-chain/project.ts) runs JSON.parse on the raw file text. readFile keeps a leading U+FEFF, JSON.parse throws on it, and the rule silently reports nothing for a package.json that starts with a byte order mark (which Node's own require() of package.json accepts). Fix: strip a leading BOM in the shared manifest and lockfile readers.

Same cause as lockfile-integrity: install-scripts.ts and readManifest call JSON.parse on text that still starts with a byte order mark, throw, and the finding is lost without any warning. Fix: strip a leading BOM when reading JSON through the shared readers.

Same cause as lockfile-integrity: readManifest returns null for a package.json with a leading byte order mark, so git, tarball and http dependencies go unreported. Fix: strip a leading BOM in readManifest.

By design, not a defect: the rule measures size in source lines, so inserting blank lines changes the number in its message (351+ becomes 702+) and can move a component over its threshold. Blank lines are not semantics-preserving for a line-count rule; the oracle cannot tell. Revisit if the rule should count only lines of code.
By design, not a defect: same as the blank-lines entry, comment lines count towards the rule's line total and appear in its message.

Quadratic in the number of dependencies: findKeyLine (src/plugin/supply-chain/project.ts) splits the whole package.json into lines and tries a RegExp on each line, once per flagged dependency. 5000 flagged dependencies take about 2.2 s. Fix: build one key-to-line index per file and reuse it.

Quadratic in the length of the literal: a secret-named variable (apiKey, password, Authorization) assigned a string of repeated '<' takes about 180 ms at 20000 characters and 730 ms at 40000 (measured per statement; the same string in other positions is instant). Unlikely in real code, but it is a regex backtracking cost in the secret heuristics (src/plugin/secrets, src/plugin/secret-heuristics.ts); cap the length the heuristics inspect.

Upstream eslint-plugin-vue rule, quadratic in the size of one template expression: a 3000-term sum (11.8 KiB) takes about 1.6 s with only this rule enabled, against 9 ms of parsing (found by re-linting with one rule at a time). Not Vue Doctor code; report upstream or disable the rule for generated templates.

Upstream eslint-plugin-vue rule that scales badly with the number of slot templates in one component: 1500 slots (125 KiB) take about 0.5 s on top of 0.1 s of parsing. Not Vue Doctor code; report upstream.
